headline: SILVER ROCKETS 2.2% TO $52.67 AS GOLD FADES NEAR $4,000 — RATIO COMPRESSION FLASHES PRECIOUS METALS RECALIBRATION
snippet: Silver surged 2.2% to US$52.67 per ounce on November 11 while gold stabilized around $4,034 — compressing the gold/silver ratio sharply in silver's favour after Monday's CPI-shock selloff hit both metals. The outperformance reverses weeks of silver lagging gold and analysts are reading it as a signal that retail and industrial buyers are stepping in at the discount: silver's industrial demand base in solar panels and EVs provides a price floor that pure monetary metals lack, and the one-day divergence suggests the rotation is broadening beyond gold.

headline: CME GROUP PLANS PHYSICALLY BACKED URANIUM FUTURES — thin $91/lb market to get institutional-grade price discovery
snippet: CME Group announced November 11 its plan to launch a physically settled uranium futures contract to improve price transparency in a market currently dominated by the thinly traded, financially settled UxC U3O8 future (UX) with under 350 lots of open interest. A physically backed contract mirrors how CME handles copper and other metals, letting participants make and take delivery rather than cash-settling against a price index — a structure institutional buyers and nuclear utilities have long requested as spot uranium tests 19-year highs near $91 per pound.

headline: GDXJ SITS 40% BELOW ITS 2026 HIGH while gold holds $4,100 — cost and liquidity repricing, not capitulation
snippet: An in-depth Discovery Alert analysis argues that the junior gold miner ETF GDXJ's 40% decline from its 2026 peak — even as spot gold remains above $4,100 — represents a structural repricing of cost inflation, financing risk and liquidity premiums rather than a true capitulation bottom. The piece distinguishes between the equity selloff (driven by labor and energy cost pressure on mine margins and tighter junior financing) and the metal's resilience (driven by central bank buying and geopolitical safe-haven demand), arguing that the gap is an investable opportunity only for companies with fully funded multi-year drill programs and sub-$1,200/oz all-in sustaining costs.

headline: YANGSHAN COPPER IMPORT PREMIUM HITS RECORD $230/TONNE — China physical tightness decouples from macro selloff
snippet: The Yangshan copper import premium — the market's real-time gauge of Chinese physical copper demand — hit a record US$230 per tonne on November 10 as SHFE-monitored warehouse inventories continued their steep 75%-plus decline from the past six months, confirming genuine industrial tightness inside China even as macro headwinds from US Fed rate-hike expectations weigh on futures prices. SP Angel's Wednesday morning view notes that Chinese manufacturers are now buying copper on confirmed orders only, a demand discipline that creates latent buying demand likely to accelerate any future sentiment recovery.

headline: COPPER HOLDS 15.6% 2026 GAIN as oil drops 7.6% and lithium craters 21% — deficit supercycle thesis intact despite CPI shock
snippet: An Averin Research commodity supercycle analysis in November 2026 highlights the remarkable resilience of copper — up 15.6% year-to-date — relative to oil (down 7.6% on Iran nuclear deal progress), lithium carbonate (down 21.1% in a month to CNY 93,500/tonne), and other raw materials facing demand slowdowns. The analysis argues the divergence validates the structural deficit thesis for copper driven by the energy transition, while warning that lithium's collapse and nickel's ongoing oversupply are reminders that not all critical minerals benefit equally from decarbonization tailwinds.

headline: SURGE BATTERY METALS REBRANDS AS LITHIUM X2 MINING — LIXX starts trading as dedicated US lithium explorer
snippet: Surge Battery Metals completed its corporate rebrand to Lithium X2 Mining on November 9, with shares now trading under the ticker LIXX to reflect the company's exclusive focus on US domestic lithium exploration led by its Nevada North Project. The rebrand comes as Washington accelerates incentives for domestically sourced battery materials under the Inflation Reduction Act, and management says the new identity is designed to sharpen investor positioning as the company advances toward a maiden resource estimate.

headline: PILBARA GOLD DRILLS 44M AT 1.00 G/T FROM 417M AT MT YORK WA — 4.2km mineralized trend confirmed at depth
snippet: Pilbara Gold (ASX: PGL) reported hole 26MYRCD084 returned 44 metres averaging 1.00 g/t gold from 417 metres depth at its Mt York project in Western Australia, confirming that the 4.2-kilometre mineralized trend extends at depth below the base of historical drilling. The result is significant because prior drilling at Mt York focused on shallower oxide targets, and the new deep hit opens a potential underground development scenario in a geological setting — the Pilbara Craton — that hosts several world-class gold systems including the Hemi discovery.

headline: ORBIT RESOURCES STARTS STAGE 2 GOODRICH PORPHYRY DRILL — partner GREAT PLAINS funds program, prior hole 136m copper-gold
snippet: Orbit Resources (ASX: OBT) has commenced Stage 2 diamond drilling at its Goodrich Porphyry Prospect in New South Wales with joint venture partner Great Plains Metals Corp (TSX-V: GPS) funding the program, following the prior campaign hole GGDD004 which returned 136.55 metres of copper-gold mineralization that validated the porphyry model. Partner-funded drilling is a critical derisking milestone for small-cap juniors: it confirms third-party validation of the geological thesis and preserves Orbit's treasury while advancing what could be a large-tonnage copper-gold system in a highly prospective jurisdiction.

headline: BELLAVISTA DRILLS 4.7M AT 9.7 G/T AND 0.7M AT 56.2 G/T AT PICKLE CROW ONTARIO — open-pittable system building grade continuity
snippet: Bellavista Resources (ASX: BVR) reported new assays from its Pickle Crow project in Ontario including 4.7 metres at 9.7 g/t gold and a 0.7-metre spike grading 56.2 g/t gold from 93 metres depth, confirming both bulk-tonnage mineralization and high-grade structural zones within the same system. Pickle Crow was a historic gold producer in northwestern Ontario and Bellavista is testing whether the deposit can support a modern open-pit scenario alongside the high-grade underground targets that made the original mine economic, with the grade combination in this result supporting both interpretations.

headline: UZBEKISTAN AIMS TO DOUBLE URANIUM OUTPUT to 15,000t/yr by 2030 — Navoiyuran expansion rattles supply forecast models
snippet: Uzbekistan's president has directed state uranium producer Navoiyuran to double annual output from approximately 7,500 tonnes to 15,000 tonnes by 2030, a plan that — if executed — would add roughly 7% to global primary uranium supply at a time when Western utilities are scrambling to source non-Russian material. The expansion relies on in-situ leaching at existing deposits and would position Uzbekistan as the world's fourth-largest uranium producer, adding a new swing variable to the supply models that currently underpin the high spot price near $91 per pound.
